pr_title: remote_server: Remove dependency on libssl and libcrypto
pr_comments:
Hey @MatthiasGrandl @huacnlee, 
This PR changes how gpui app should be initialized; it used to provide a http client by default, but we needed to make that customizable. If your apps depend on e.g. fetching images from Internet, bumping your projects past that commit might break things. You need to use `with_http_client` on App or `.set_http_client` on an AppContext. On the upside, your apps no longer need to depend on isahc if they don't need to.

I plan to merge this PR tomorrow after the releases are cut.

Hi @osiewicz 

Today, I have upgrade GPUI to latest. And then I realize that we must to `set_http_client`. Because the `img` element need, if it load image from a remote URL, that will need `cx.http_client`.

So, maybe you can consider can we have a http client in GPUI by default, then we do not need set it again.
This is precisely why we have done it. In Zed we wanted to get rid of a default http client (isahc) and instead let user pick their own.

issue_context.title: Unable to Execute zed-remote-server-stable Command on Ubuntu Server 22.04 Due to Missing libssl.so.1.1
issue_context.body:
### Check for existing issues - [X] Completed ### Describe the bug / provide steps to reproduce it When using SSH to remotely connect to an Ubuntu Server 22.04 development environment, the execution of the zed-remote-server-stable command fails due to a dependency on libssl.so.1.1, which has been deprecated in Ubuntu 22.04. #### Error Log: ```txt 2024-08-01T10:04:34.823854Z [ERROR] failed to run command: .local/zed-remote-server-stable: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libssl.so.1.1: version `OPENSSL_1_1_1' not found (required by .local/zed-remote-server-stable) ``` ### Environment no ### If applicable, add mockups / screenshots to help explain present your vision of the feature _No response_ ### If applicable, attach your Zed.log file to this issue.
Zed.log
comments: Thanks for reporting.  We had run into this internally as well.

I have run into the same while trying to debug remote dev using ssh://localhost:2222/home/me/work.
localhost is a docker container running fedora:latest image (which would be fedora 40)
Also ran into this on debian bookworm.

Not sure if this is related, but FYI I'm hitting this on Arch too even though libssl.so.1.1 is still available here:

```bash
$ ll /usr/lib/libssl.so.1.1
-rwxr-xr-x 1 root root 556792 Jul  7 02:45 /usr/lib/libssl.so.1.1

$ pacman -F /usr/lib/libssl.so.1.1
usr/lib/libssl.so.1.1 is owned by core/openssl-1.1 1.1.1.t-1

$ pacman -Qi zed
Name            : zed
Version         : 0.149.5-1
...
```
I've discovered that libssl 1.1 needs to be available on the remote server.  Once corrected, this now works.

Confirming for 

## client
```
macOS Sonoma Version 14.6.1
```

## remote
```
Distributor ID: Ubuntu
Description:    Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS
Release:        22.04
Codename:       jammy
```
